appearance.stem_hairs.prickles.density.why: A nightshade armed with prickles bears them on its young stems and leaf stalks among its hairs, as thickly as its flora says: one every few centimetres up a stem where sparse, closer where it is called prickly, crowded where densely prickly.

appearance.stem_hairs.prickles.length.why: A stem's prickles are as long as its flora states, or four millimetres where it states none.

appearance.stem_hairs.prickles.lie.why: A prickle stands out from the stem, its point bent back toward the stem's foot.

rules.note: How a nightshade's stem prickles are drawn among its stem hairs (nightshades round 5, 2026-10-18/19), choices of the model's: about one prickle per few square centimetres where sparse (Flora of China's eggplant, sparingly armed), more where prickly or densely so; four millimetres long where no length is stated, near Flora of China's 3 mm calyx prickles; each bent back toward the stem's foot, as floras' recurved prickles are. Homed at the family, not at all plants: roses' and brambles' prickles wait for a shared armature module (Joshi, 2026-10-19 06:14Z).

traits.leaf_incision.note: Lucid family key, Solanaceae (read 2026-10-17): leaves sometimes deeply lobed (pinnatifid to tripinnatifid); DELTA, Solanaceae (read 2026-10-17): lamina entire or dissected, pinnatifid when cut; Flora of China (read 2026-10-17): some Solanum much divided or lobed.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Flora of China, Solanaceae (read 2026-10-17): blade entire, dentate, lobed or divided; berry-fruited groups entire. Lucid family key (read 2026-10-17): entire, dentate, serrate, sinuate or spiny. Weighted by genus: most Solanum, Cestrum, Lycium blades are entire or wavy; coarse teeth in Physalis, Datura, Nicotiana parts.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Lucid family key, Solanaceae (read 2026-10-17): blade or lobe outlines filiform to linear, lanceolate, ovate, elliptic, oblanceolate, oblong, orbicular. Ranking ours, weighted by genus: Solanum (c. 1,500 species per Wikipedia Solanum (read 2026-10-17); most of the family per Wikipedia Solanaceae) has mostly ovate to elliptic blades, as do Cestrum and Physalis; narrow in Lycium.

traits.stamens.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 428: stamens 5, rarely 4 or 2 plus 2 staminodes, on the corolla tube.

traits.corolla_shape.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 428: perianth usually tubular, rotate or salverform, no order given (Floral Diagrams p. 315-317: long tubes or trumpets; Solanum short with reflexed lobes).

traits.hypanthium.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 428: Simpson states the hypanthium is absent.

traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 321 Solanaceae (order Solanales): herbaceous or woody; leaves alternate, simple; no stipules; flowers mostly regular; calyx 4- to 6-lobed, persisting; corolla united, usually 5-lobed; stamens on the corolla tube, alternate with its lobes; ovary of two cells, superior (the order's 'ovary superior'); fruit a capsule or a berry. Some (Schizanthus, Salpiglossis) are irregular.

traits.rosette.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Solanaceae as that work draws it, there coded together with Duckeodendraceae, Goetzeaceae, Nolanaceae: whether the leaves gather in rosettes (character 22), coded often a basal rosette, often no rosette, rarely rosettes at the stem tips. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.life_span.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Solanaceae as that work draws it, there coded together with Duckeodendraceae, Goetzeaceae, Nolanaceae: the herbs' life form (character 21), coded often annual, often biennial, often perennial. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.zygomorphy.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Solanaceae with Duckeodendraceae, Goetzeaceae, Nolanaceae: its irregular flowers are of no named kind (pea flower, two lips, orchid lip), read from the coded corolla symmetry (spec-rework/b1/delta): zygomorphy other. Its flowers are not mostly zygomorphic, so a plant of it states its own symmetry; one that is zygomorphic draws this kind, and one stating none is drawn regular.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 428, 429, family Solanaceae: phyllotaxis pattern spiral, usually; read as {"spiral": "usually"}.

traits.inflorescence.note: DELTA Solanaceae (read 2026-10-17): flowers solitary or grouped, the grouped units apparently cymose; Wikipedia (read 2026-10-17) agrees (solitary or cymose). Weighted by genus size (approximate): Solanum (~1,250) bears flowers in leaf-opposed or extra-axillary cymes, as do Cestrum and Nicotiana; solitary or fascicled flowers mark Physalis, Capsicum, Datura, Lycium and many Lycianthes (a few hundred spp). Re-ranks the earlier value, from plant-systematics-simpson, whose top states were tied.

traits.sexual_system.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 428, 429, family Solanaceae: sexual system hermaphrodite; read as "hermaphrodite".

traits.fruit_type.note: Wikipedia Solanaceae (read 2026-10-17; ~2,700 spp): berries across Solanoideae (bar Datura and Hyoscyameae), Juanulloideae and Cestrum; capsules in the rest of Cestroideae, Schizanthoideae, Salpiglossideae, Datura; drupes in Lycieae and Iochrominae. DELTA (read 2026-10-17) lists capsule, berry or drupe. Weighted by genus size (approximate, not read this session): berry-fruited Solanum (~1,250) alone is nearly half the family, plus Lycianthes (~200), Cestrum (~150), Physalis, Capsicum; capsular Nicotiana (~75), Petunia, Schizanthus, Datura total a few hundred. Re-ranks the earlier value, from plant-systematics-simpson, whose top states were tied.

traits.leaf_division.note: Added kinds only; the usual kind's source is the family's `traits` note. The books add compound (sometimes): Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 428, 429: simple, pinnate or ternate.

generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the herb base: a nightshade's stem is a sympodium, each unit ending in an inflorescence that the next unit pushes aside, so its flowers stand beside the stem across from a leaf or in the forks of its branches.
